items.title: Oil edges down as investors await US midterm election results
items.description: Oil prices decreased due to investor caution ahead of the US midterm elections and ongoing peace negotiations. Brent futures and West Texas Intermediate crude both saw declines despite an unexpected drop in US crude stocks. Vote counting for the midterm elections continues, which may influence the Republican party's control of Congress. Peace talks in the Middle East were also impacted, especially involving the US and Iran.

items.title: Positive Breakout: These 8 stocks cross above their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty200 pack, eight stocks' closing prices crossed above their 200-day moving averages (DMA) on November 3, 2026, according to StockEdge's technical scan data. The 200-day moving average (DMA) is used by traders as a key indicator for determining the overall trend of a stock. As long as a stock's price remains above its 200-day moving average on the daily timeframe, it is generally interpreted as being in an overall uptrend.

items.title: RBI's Rs 50,000 crore VRRR faces muted response from market
items.description: The Reserve Bank of India announced a variable rate reverse repo operation of ₹50,000 crore. This decision came after the banking system liquidity reached nearly ₹2 lakh crore on Monday. Banks opted to bid ₹23,905 crore, reflecting an asymmetry in the banking system's surplus. The weighted average call rate decreased to 5.45% from 5.50% on Monday. Another VRRR operation of ₹50,000 crore is scheduled for Wednesday.

items.title: Sensex, Nifty soar to a two-month high as FPIs ramp up buying activity
items.description: Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty closed at their highest levels in nearly two months. Foreign investors have been net buying Indian equities, contributing to market gains over the past sessions. HDFC Bank was a significant contributor to the Nifty's gains, along with other major stocks like ICICI Bank. Decreasing crude oil prices have improved market sentiment among investors recently.

items.title: Sebi imposes Rs 40 lakh penalty on two brokers in Axis Mutual Fund front-running case
items.description: Securities and Exchange Board of India has imposed penalties on two stockbroking firms over regulatory violations. Woodstock Broking and Marfatia Stock Broking allowed unauthorized access to their trading terminals. This access facilitated front-running trades by Prijesh Kurani, who operated from Dubai. The investigation revealed insider information was shared regarding Axis Mutual Fund's trades. The regulatory body emphasized the importance of stringent controls over terminal access and trading infrastructure.

items.title: D-Street braces for weak opening on negative GIFT Nifty cues
items.description: Benchmark Nifty increased by 1.6% to close at 23,810 following an extended rally. This upward trend was influenced by easing crude prices and continuous foreign fund inflows. Analysts expect Indian equities to consolidate positively after a sharp recovery in recent sessions. The rupee appreciated by 9 paise against the US dollar amid substantial buying in domestic equity markets. India VIX rose by 1.

items.title: Stocks in news: NSE, BSE, SBI, Happiest Minds, MCX, IEX and Minda Corp
items.description: The Indian stock market continues its upward momentum, with the Nifty 50 showing a robust rally and hitting significant resistance levels. Major players like NSE and SBI have posted remarkable quarterly results, illustrating their strong profitability and revenue growth. Firms such as Happiest Minds Technologies and the Multi Commodity Exchange of India contributed positively to the market's performance.

items.title: US mid-terms may help D-Street break free from geopolitical overhang
items.description: The upcoming US mid-term elections will potentially influence global markets and trade policies. Investors are closely watching whether the outcomes will ease uncertainties regarding tariffs and immigration. The results could shape the policy direction and affect the sentiment of global investors. Analysts suggest that the focus should remain on domestic earnings growth and financial flows.

items.title: Irdai mandates four-tier structure for motor insurance from Dec 15
items.description: Irdai will implement a four-tier structure for motor insurance covering private cars and two-wheelers. Customers will have the option to select separate covers, including mandatory third-party liability and optional personal accident cover. Existing policyholders can add occupant liability coverage without canceling their current policies.

items.title: Lenders accept Supreme Housing's Rs 522-crore settlement offer
items.description: Canara Bank along with other lenders accepted a ₹522-crore one time settlement offer from Supreme Housing and Hospitality. This settlement will help the company resolve debts close to ₹700 crore, representing a 75% recovery for involved banks. The one-time settlement includes both fund and non-fund exposure from corporate guarantees given to subsidiary entities.

items.title: NBFCs redesign lending models ahead of revolving credit curbs
items.description: Non-banking financial companies are innovating loan products to align with upcoming Reserve Bank of India guidelines. These guidelines aim to limit revolving credit facilities, prompting firms to develop term loans. Bajaj Finance has already begun launching new term loan variants, while Tata Capital is testing modified flexi-loan products. Other NBFCs are reviewing their positions on revolving credit exposure ahead of the final regulations.

items.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Thursday
items.description: Indian markets extended their rally, with Sensex gaining 384 points to 77,301 and Nifty rising 150 points to 23,961, marking two-month highs. Positive sentiment, strong earnings, festive demand and buying across mid- and small-caps supported gains.

items.title: Strong balance sheet, domestic focus, and a moat matter more: 5 large-cap stocks with upside potential of up to 24%
items.description: The big event the market was waiting for has come and gone. So, is there greater clarity about where the crisis in the Gulf is headed? Not really. While US President Trump acknowledged the war was one of the reasons his Republican party received a drubbing at the hands of the Democrats, he said he would do it again. Which suggests it is unlikely that the uncertainty and volatility in the markets will go away anytime soon.

items.title: Ather Energy among 15 stocks that hit 52-week highs and rallied up to 30% in a month
items.description: On Wednesday, the benchmark Sensex gained 384 points to close at 77,301. Amid the market rally, 15 stocks from the BSE 500 Index touched fresh 52-week highs, marking their highest price levels in the past year. A 52-week high represents the highest price at which a stock has traded over the previous year and can indicate increased market activity and investor interest.

items.title: Sebi initiates action against 8 investment advisers over non-payment of renewal fees
items.description: SEBI has initiated proceedings against eight registered investment advisers for failing to pay mandatory renewal fees. The defaults span 2018 to 2024, with the regulator seeking explanations and warning of possible suspension or cancellation of registrations.

items.title: Sebi sets up working group to review Innovators Growth Platform framework
items.description: SEBI has formed a working group to review Innovators Growth Platform regulations and improve capital access for startups. The panel will examine listing eligibility, fundraising, investor participation, disclosures and migration to mainboards while safeguarding investor interests.

items.title: Sebi eases KYC norms for NRIs, OCIs, allows digital onboarding from December 3
items.description: SEBI has relaxed KYC requirements for NRIs, OCIs and foreign nationals, allowing eligible overseas clients in FATF-compliant countries to complete onboarding digitally. The revised framework introduces video verification, electronic documents and simplified repeat KYC, effective December 3, 2026.

items.title: Market wrap: BEL, Adani Ent, TCS, HCL Tech top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Wednesday
items.description: Indian equity markets advanced for the fifth consecutive session as easing crude oil prices and US-Iran diplomatic hopes boosted sentiment. Nifty gained 150 points, while Sensex rose 383 points, led by realty, metal and consumer durables stocks.

items.title: Sebi cancels registrations of 8 investment advisers for non-payment of renewal fees
items.description: Sebi has announced relaxed KYC requirements for Non-Resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India, and foreign nationals. These changes will allow them to complete digital onboarding from FATF-compliant countries effectively. Intermediaries can accept KYC submissions without requiring physical presence in India. Video In-Person Verification is now permitted where in-person verification isn't feasible, enhancing compliance capabilities. The revised framework, effective from December 3, is aimed at simplifying the entire onboarding process.

items.title: Auto sales growth to cool post-festive season, says Monarch; bets on Minda Corp, RK Forgings and Sundram Fasteners
items.description: Auto sales growth is expected to moderate in the second half of FY27 after strong festive demand, while tractor sales may remain weak. Monarch Networth Capital prefers diversified ancillary players Minda Corporation, RK Forgings and Sundram Fasteners, with potential upside of up to 44%.

items.title: Stock Radar: Down over 25% from highs! CDSL stock showing signs of bottoming out; time to buy?
items.description: CDSL has rebounded from the lower boundary of its four-year ascending channel and reclaimed key moving averages, indicating improving momentum. Experts see a potential rise toward Rs 1,450 over the next three to four weeks, with a stop-loss below Rs 1,110.

items.title: 12 BSE 500 stocks defy market trend, rally up to 65% in 3 months
items.description: While the benchmark index declined nearly 2% over the past three months, the BSE 500 index slipped around 5%, reflecting broader weakness in the market. Several BSE 500 stocks witnessed sharp corrections during this period. However, a handful of stocks bucked the trend and delivered impressive gains. We highlight 12 BSE 500 stocks that rallied between 25% and 65% over the past three months, defying the broader market trend. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: Kopsi, Taiwan, other Asian stocks tumble after US midterm elections signal Democratic victory. What’s the connection?
items.description: South Korean and Taiwanese equities tumbled as a potential Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections fuelled concerns over tighter AI regulations and slower data centre investments. Chipmakers led the sell-off, dragging regional markets lower, while Asian currencies strengthened against a weaker dollar.

items.title: Equitas Small Finance Bank shares jump 9% after Balaji Nuthalapadi’s appointment as interim CEO
items.description: The bank further said that appointment of Nuthalapadi as interim CEO, consequent to the resignation of P. N. Vasudevan as the MD & CEO, shall take effect from the date of RBI approval or such other date as may be stipulated by the RBI in this regard.

items.title: Democrats’ win rattles Trump trades from AI stocks to crypto
items.description: The recent Democratic majority in Congress triggered a downturn in global markets, most notably impacting technology stocks. Investors are now wary about President Trump’s policies and their implications for AI investments. Conversely, solar stocks saw an uptick, signaling potential changes to clean energy regulations. Additionally, Treasury yields dropped as heightened oversight dampens fiscal stimulus hopes, while cryptocurrencies also fell amid uncertainty surrounding upcoming industry regulations.

items.title: Diwali 2026: Will Sensex, Nifty reclaim their peaks or scale new highs? Analysts map the road ahead
items.description: Market analysts are tentatively optimistic about Indian equity markets seeing a resurgence in the next financial year. Expectations suggest that both the Sensex and Nifty may rise to their past peak levels by Diwali 2027, driven by improving corporate profitability. While favorable valuations and steady domestic investments bolster this outlook, global uncertainties like inflation, interest rates, and oil prices could pose challenges.

items.title: BLS Polymers shares rally 6% after strong stock market debut
items.description: BLS Polymers shares extended their strong debut gains, rising nearly 6% on Wednesday after listing at a 65% premium to the IPO price. The issue received 241 times subscription, while the company reported higher income and profit in FY26.

items.title: ITC shares jump 6% in two days after Q2 results. More upside ahead?
items.description: ITC shares rose to Rs 283.5 apiece on NSE on Wednesday morning, the highest level seen by the stock in nearly three months. The stock has now recovered more than 12% in five sessions after hitting a 52-week low of Rs 253 apiece in late October.
